Flu season does not wait, and neither is Nuevo Laredo. The municipal government has announced a free, two-day vaccination drive — influenza, pneumococcus and COVID-19 — running this Friday and Saturday ahead of the winter respiratory-illness surge, according to Central de Noticias Tamaulipas, reporting the city's official announcement.

The campaign, organized by the Secretaría de Bienestar Social and the municipal Health Department, will run Friday, October 23 and Saturday, October 24, from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the Explanada Esteban Baca Calderón, on Avenida Guerrero between Héroe de Nacataz and Maclovio Herrera streets.

The headline feature is the drive-thru format: residents can get vaccinated without leaving their cars, with no limit on the number of people per vehicle. A walk-up module will also serve anyone arriving on foot or by public transit.

The doses are open to everyone aged six months and older. Adults need an official ID; minors are advised — but not required — to bring their vaccination card so records can be updated. Everyone vaccinated receives an official proof of vaccination.

City health authorities project about 1,000 vaccinations per day — roughly 2,000 doses across the two days — and are urging residents to take advantage of the campaign before seasonal respiratory illnesses climb.

For a border city where thousands cross daily and winter crowds gather fast, two days of free, no-appointment shots in the middle of downtown is exactly the kind of prevention that pays off.

Sources: Central de Noticias Tamaulipas (Oct. 21, 2026), reporting the Gobierno Municipal de Nuevo Laredo announcement.

title: Free shots, no appointment: Nuevo Laredo launches drive-thru vaccination weekend
